_comment: S3b Negative-DT Boundary — companion attribute study to S3 (R&R-003, GitHub #1). Defined 2026-06-06.
_status: BUILT, NOT YET RUN. Updated 2026-08-19 (Route B, §8 steps 2-4). synth/modulator.py now supports extended=True (contracts C1/C2): negative dt_s renders genuinely early audio instead of clamping to zero; tests/test_modulator.py:73 was REPLACED (not deleted) by test_negative_dt_shifts_signal_earlier. harness/run_scenario.py's hard-exit is REMOVED; this scenario now sets "requires_extended_dt": true, which routes it through the extended playback path (early-armed via _wait_for_cycle's early_by_s). run_study.py's _SCENARIO_REGISTRY registration is C4 (see that file). Offline placement proof (G1/G2, no decoder, no device): g1_g2_full_grid_placement_check.py — all 10 parts place to one sample, byte-identical across two runs. G3 (WSJT-X self-validation over the full grid) WAVs rendered by g3_full_grid_self_validation_render.py; GUI confirmation is a manual step (Captain's, per gate_render.py's existing convention) and has NOT been performed as of this note. G4 (>=95% decode at dt_s=0) not yet measured — requires a live run. STILL NOT RUN: needs the Captain's hardware (Voicemeeter AUX Input routing, per the standing capture-endpoint note) and an HK-013 supervisor for the ~4.2 h unattended sizing below.
_status_warning: The description field below repeats a product finding from run aa053a9 ('OpenWSFZ still decodes most negative-DT signals but reports DT ~= 0') that is VOID: the pre-2026-08-19 clamp meant those parts were DT=0 audio and the decoder was correct. Do not cite it as a product finding — the negative-DT decode boundary is genuinely UNMEASURED until this scenario actually runs.
_sizing_note: Route B spec §4 (HK-021(m)/(o) applied before running): 3 trials/part gives a decode-rate SE of ~29pp at p=0.5 -- cannot resolve a knee at all. Corrected to 100 trials/part below (1.96*SE ~= 9.8pp at p=0.5, tighter at the extremes) -- the MECHANICALLY required floor for this response, not a preference. At 10 parts x 100 trials x 2 appraisers x 15s, this is ~4.2h unattended (HK-013 supervisor + UTC-midnight rotation guard required). Spec: 'if 4.2 hours is not acceptable, cut PARTS, not TRIALS... bring me the tradeoff rather than splitting the difference' -- that choice (which 5 of the 10 parts to keep, if any are cut) is reserved for the Architect/Captain, not decided here. All 10 parts are left in place pending that call.
name: Negative-DT decode boundary
description: 10 parts × 2 appraisers × 3 trials. Companion to the redesigned S3: sweeps DT from 0.0 down to −2.7 s in 0.3 s steps and measures DECODE RATE (attribute: did the message decode? yes/no) rather than DT precision. Cleanly separates the question 'does it decode?' from 'does it report DT accurately?' — both questions were conflated in the original S3 design. The product finding from run aa053a9 is that OpenWSFZ still decodes most negative-DT signals (decode rate ≈ near-perfect even for parts 0–3) but reports DT ≈ 0 regardless of the true offset; this study measures the decode half of that finding. Analysis: per-part decode rate per appraiser; reported as an informational table, not a Gage R&R. See STUDY-SPEC §6 and §16.
harness_note: Negative DT means the transmitter fires before the nominal slot boundary. "requires_extended_dt": true (above) routes this scenario through synth.modulator.modulate's extended=True contract (C1/C2) -- the returned buffer genuinely contains early audio, and harness/run_scenario.py's main loop arms playback `-buffer_start_s` seconds before the nominal cycle boundary (early_by_s, via _wait_for_cycle). Analysis key: matched (decoded) vs missed (not decoded) per (part, appraiser) — DO NOT compute Gage R&R on the DT response for this scenario.
